h1: The 7 Best Bluetooth Computer Mice for Laptops, Tablets and Quiet Desks, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Bluetooth Computer Mice: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 Bluetooth mice with no-dongle and dual-mode designs, scored on battery, click noise, device switching and size.
summary: The Logitech M720 Triathlon is the best Bluetooth mouse for people who juggle devices, remembering three computers with a 24 month battery claim. The Logitech Signature M550 L is the pick for large hands, the M240 is the quiet no-dongle travel mouse, and the TECKNET and Afaartcci add a USB receiver as a fallback.
intro: Bluetooth mice solve one problem and create another. They free the USB port, which matters on a slim laptop with two ports, but a Bluetooth link must be re-established after sleep, and a mouse that takes a few seconds to wake feels worse than a dongle that never does. Whether that trade suits you depends on how often you wake the machine and how many devices share the mouse.

We ranked seven Bluetooth mice by battery life, click noise, multi-device support, size and whether a USB receiver backs up the Bluetooth link. We reviewed listings, treating the battery claims, such as 18 months, as manufacturer figures that depend on use. Hand size matters more than any spec, so we flag which models run small and which run large.

products.name: Logitech M720 Triathlon Multi-Device Mouse
products.verdict: Bluetooth or USB receiver, switching between devices, with a 24 month battery claim.
products.description:
The M720 Triathlon connects over Bluetooth or a USB-A receiver, works across computers, laptops and tablets, has hyper-fast scrolling and a 24 month battery life per the listing. It is a full-size right-handed mouse and costs $25 to $50.

It wins because switching a single mouse between a desktop, a laptop and a tablet is the best reason to buy Bluetooth, and this mouse is built for it. The two-year battery claim means almost no maintenance. The full-size shape suits most hands.

Buy it for a multi-device desk. It is right-handed only.
products.idealFor: People who use a desktop, laptop and tablet during the same day.

products.name: Logitech Signature M550 L Bluetooth Mouse
products.verdict: A full-size silent mouse with a soft thumb area, rubber grips and a 2 year battery claim.
products.description:
The Signature M550 L is a large-size Bluetooth mouse with silent clicks, a soft thumb area, rubber side grips and a battery life of two years per the listing. The price is under $25.

The runner-up spot suits it because comfort over long sessions comes from size and grip, and this mouse has both for large hands. Silent clicks help in shared rooms. It has no receiver option.

Buy it for big hands and long days. If your hand is small, take a compact mouse.
products.idealFor: Large hands and long desk sessions.
products.skipIf: You have small hands or travel light.

products.name: Logitech M240 Silent Bluetooth Mouse
products.verdict: Compact, no dongle, clicks claimed 90 percent quieter and up to 18 months of battery.
products.description:
The M240 is a compact Bluetooth mouse with no USB receiver, clicks claimed to be 90 percent quieter, auto sleep and up to 18 months of battery. It costs under $25.

Third place fits because it suits a laptop bag and a quiet room. Auto sleep saves battery, though waking takes a moment. It is small for large hands.

Buy it for a laptop and quiet spaces.
products.idealFor: Laptop and tablet owners who want a quiet mouse with no dongle.

products.name: TECKNET Dual-Mode Bluetooth Wireless Mouse
products.verdict: Bluetooth plus a 2.4G USB receiver, five DPI levels to 4000 and remembered settings.
products.description:
The TECKNET dual-mode mouse offers Bluetooth 5.2/3.0 and a 2.4G USB-A receiver, five DPI levels from 800 to 4000, textured rubber grips and a memory that retains the DPI setting. It costs under $25.

Fourth place suits it because two connection modes let it serve a laptop over Bluetooth and a desktop through the dongle. Remembering DPI saves resetting. Battery life is not listed.

Buy it for a two-device home on a budget.
products.idealFor: Two-device households on a modest budget.
products.skipIf: You want a stated battery life.

products.name: Lenovo WL310 Bluetooth Silent Mouse
products.verdict: Bluetooth 5.0, silent clicks and three DPI levels in an ergonomic shape.
products.description:
The Lenovo WL310 uses Bluetooth 5.0, has silent clicks, three DPI levels (1000, 1200, 1600) and an ergonomic, portable shape. It costs under $25.

Fifth place goes to it because it offers a little more shape than a travel mouse with quiet clicks. Battery life is not listed.

Buy it for a quiet shared desk.
products.idealFor: Quiet shared spaces and users who want more shape than a travel mouse.
products.skipIf: You want a stated battery life.

products.name: Afaartcci Rechargeable Silent Bluetooth Mouse
products.verdict: Bluetooth and 2.4G, silent buttons and a 500mAh battery that charges in two hours.
products.description:
This mouse has Bluetooth 5.2/3.0 and a 2.4G USB receiver, silent buttons, LED lights and a 500mAh battery that refills in roughly two hours and runs for a bit over a week, with a month of standby. It costs under $25.

Sixth place fits because a weekly charge is a chore next to a battery that lasts a year or two. It suits people who prefer not to buy cells.

Buy it if you do not mind charging.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who want Bluetooth plus a receiver and do not mind charging.

products.name: Logitech M196 Compact Bluetooth Mouse
products.verdict: An ambidextrous contoured mouse with no receiver, light enough for any bag.
products.description:
The M196 is a compact Bluetooth mouse with no receiver, an ambidextrous contoured shape, line-by-line scrolling and optical tracking, aimed at laptops and tablets. It costs under $25.

Last place reflects its plain spec sheet, with no battery claim. Ambidextrous design suits left-handers.

Buy it for a simple, light travel mouse.
products.idealFor: Left-handers and travelers who want the simplest Bluetooth mouse.

whatMatters.detail: Bluetooth-only mice free the USB port but can lag after sleep. Dual-mode mice add a receiver for desktops. Check for a 2.4G receiver in the listing.
Some mice remember several devices and switch with a button. That suits desk, laptop and tablet users. Look for multi-device in the listing.
Cell-powered mice claim months to two years, and rechargeable ones last days. Claims depend on use. Prefer a stated figure.
Silent switches cut click noise, useful in libraries and shared homes. Check for quiet or silent clicks.
A mouse should fit your hand. Compact ones suit small hands and travel, large ones suit big hands. Ambidextrous shapes help left-handers.

faq.q: Why does my Bluetooth mouse lag after sleep?
faq.a: It has to reconnect. Click or move it and wait a moment. A dual-mode mouse with a receiver avoids it.
Buying a Bluetooth-only mouse for a desktop without Bluetooth. Check your computer first.

faq.q: Is Bluetooth better than a dongle?
faq.a: It frees a port but may reconnect slower. A dongle is steadier.
Turn on the mouse, hold the pairing button, open Bluetooth settings and choose it.

faq.q: Does a silent mouse feel different?
faq.a: Clicks are softer, with less snap. Most people adapt quickly.

faq.q: How long do the cells last?
faq.a: Claims run from 18 to 24 months, depending on use. Replace when the cursor stutters.

finalTake: The Logitech M720 Triathlon is the best Bluetooth mouse for multi-device users, with long battery life and a receiver option. The M550 L suits large hands, the M240 is the quiet travel pick, and the TECKNET and Afaartcci are cheap dual-mode options.
